confirmed.statement: Check (a): the paper states random assignment once, in the Design section: 'Participants were randomly assigned to one of three learning groups: human-only (control condition; n=64), general-AI (n=67), or regulated-AI (n=65).' The form's assignment quote matches this sentence word for word, and its locator is right. The abstract does not say 'random', which explains the search record's 'RCT?' label. The full text settles it.

confirmed.statement: unit 'individual' rests on the subject of that sentence ('Participants were randomly assigned'). The paper does not say how it randomized (no method, blocking, or allocation ratio). Participants came in sessions of up to five, and 'the experimenter verbally reinforced all task instructions'. The paper does not say whether one session mixed conditions. If whole sessions shared a condition, assignment was clustered and codebook section 10 would apply. The form's notes already record this gap, so no coded value changes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Design; p. 12, Procedure ('Participants were run in groups of up to five per session in a lab setting'); p. 13, Procedure

confirmed.statement: The preliminary analyses fit random assignment. The groups did not differ in baseline AUT fluency, F(2, 193) = 0.30, p = .74, or flexibility, F(2, 193) = 0.32, p = .73, or in prior ChatGPT experience, chi-square(10, N = 196) = 8.35, p = .60.

confirmed.statement: Check (b): the assigned treatment is access to ChatGPT for the participant's own solution. The product improvement task was 'completed independently in the control condition versus with ChatGPT assistance in both AI groups'. Each participant wrote and submitted one idea, and two experts scored 'all (100%) of the 196 scripts blind to experimental condition'. No condition differs only in whose output gets rated.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 8-9, Design; p. 14, Intervention Stage; p. 15, Scoring Procedure; Appendix A, pp. 33-35

confirmed.statement: Check (c): the tool is a large language model. The paper calls ChatGPT 'a generative AI-based large language model (LLM)'. The Reproducibility Note says both AI groups 'used the GPT-4 version of ChatGPT via the web interface' through a ChatGPT Plus subscription, with default parameters and memory/model training switched off. ai_tool.name_model matches.

confirmed.statement: Check (d), control arm: human-only is a no-AI control with no other aid. It 'had no other open tabs or windows' and 'solved the task independently', with the same task overview and the same 12 minutes. So arms[human-only].ai = 'none' and the two ai_vs_bau contrasts against it are right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Design ('control condition'); p. 13, Procedure; p. 14, Intervention Stage; Fig. 1, p. 13; Appendix A, pp. 33-34

confirmed.statement: Check (d), AI arms: both used the same ChatGPT-4 in a split-screen window on the same 12-minute task. General-AI used it 'in any way they liked'. Regulated-AI had Phase 1 (3 min, own ideas, 'independently'), Phase 2 (6 min with ChatGPT and seven sample prompts, own prompts allowed) and Phase 3 (3 min to 'independently refine and submit'). The arms descriptions match these passages. Coding regulated-AI vs general-AI as ai_design, with the proposed configuration as treatment and free use as control, follows codebook section 5. Whether ChatGPT stayed open in Phase 3 is an outcome-level question that the form's open_questions already raise.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 14, Intervention Stage; p. 9 and Table 1, p. 10 (seven sample prompts); Fig. 1, p. 13; Appendix A, pp. 34-35

confirmed.statement: Caveat, no coded value changes: regulated-AI vs human-only is ai_vs_bau under codebook section 5, but that arm bundles ChatGPT with the think-first protocol and the sample prompts. The paper names the missing control itself: learners who 'received the same guided approach and sample prompts as the regulated-AI group during the intervention but did not interact with ChatGPT', a proposed 'regulated-human' group. The form's open_questions raise bundling only for the regulated vs general contrast. Criterion 1 does not depend on this arm, because general-AI vs human-only is randomized on its own.

summary: The PDF states that participants were randomly assigned to a no-AI control, to free use of ChatGPT-4, or to a guided 'think first, ChatGPT later' use of ChatGPT-4 for their own product improvement idea (p. 8; p. 14), and every value in assignment, arms, and ai_tool matches the text. Two caveats change no coded value: the paper does not say how it randomized or whether sessions of up to five mixed conditions (the form's notes record this), and the regulated-AI arm bundles ChatGPT with a guided protocol that, as the paper says itself, has no matched non-AI control (p. 32).
